features.title: Start time and duration on every tool call
features.summary: Each tool card in the chat transcript, native or plugin-owned, root or nested, shows how long the call took and when it started ("1.2 s · 14:02:11"). Wait calls also show elapsed time and an indeterminate bar, or a timeout countdown bar when an explicit limit is set. Users can interrupt through the existing composer controls.

configuration.constraints: Boolean; show the timing line on tool cards.
How the start time reads: clock time (with the day when not today) or relative to now.

failureModes: No call time is shown while the model is still writing the arguments.
A result whose call fell outside the loaded history shows only when it ended.

If DSH stops rendering tool cards through the keyed tool-call renderer and its renderSlot dispatch, the line disappears and the browser console logs one @dshfiles/tool-meta warning; the cards themselves are untouched.

onboarding.firstAction: Ask the agent for a task that runs a tool.
onboarding.doneWhen: Each tool card shows when it started and how long it took.

telemetry.reason: Client-only: Start time and duration on every tool call renders browser state and starts no Host work of its own.

features.title: File reads as a syntax-highlighted code card
features.summary: A settled `read` renders as the shared CodeBlock instead of the native preview: the header names the file and how much of it this window holds ("Showing 40 of 210 lines"), the gutter counts from the offset the call asked for, the grammar follows the file extension, and wrap, copy and an open-at-the-line path are there. The card starts closed, a long window scrolls inside it, and a failed, running, nested or metadata-less read keeps the native row.
features.currentSurface: transcript: file read as a code card

configuration.constraints: Boolean; show a `read` result as a code card instead of the native row.

failureModes: A read whose result metadata is missing (a replayed call from before the metadata existed) keeps the native row.
A window the read tool cut by bytes but not by lines still renders; the footer line the tool appended is part of the model-facing text, not of the card.
The card highlights through the Host grammars, so an extension with no grammar renders as plain text.
Nested calls inside a `workflow` or subagent call keep the native row.

telemetry.reason: Client-only: the read card renders already-persisted tool metadata and starts no Host work of its own.

features.title: File edits as collapsible diffs
features.summary: A settled `edit` or `write` and every stage of an `apply_patch` render as one card with the added/removed totals and one collapsible unified diff per hunk, through the shared PatchView. A failed apply_patch shows its rejection text. Calls with no applied hunks (a running edit, a failed one) keep the native row; `apply_patch` has no native card, so it always uses this one.
features.currentSurface: transcript: file edit as a collapsible diff

configuration.constraints: Boolean; show `edit` / `write` as a diff card instead of the native row. `apply_patch` keeps its diff either way, because DSH has no other card for it.

failureModes: A `apply_patch` call whose arguments left the loaded history shows its recorded result text instead of the hunks.

The hunk text the tools persist is the change plus three context lines, so a collapsed context block cannot be expanded into the rest of the file here; the review surfaces do that from full file contents.
A write whose metadata lists no hunk (a new file, an identical overwrite) shows its whole content as additions.
A field of the applied metadata this model cannot decode keeps the native row.

telemetry.reason: Client-only: the diff card parses persisted tool metadata in the browser and starts no Host work.

features.title: The native approval request as a risk card
features.summary: A native approval request renders in the composer as one card: a risk badge (Destructive for a command that deletes, overwrites or publishes, Read-only for a tool that only reads, Review otherwise), the tool name, the request's reason, the command the call runs, and Reject / Allow once with the Esc and Enter keys. The decision still goes through the native approval package's answer, so its waterfall, withdrawal and one-answer lock are unchanged; turning the card off shows the native panel.

configuration.constraints: Boolean; off hands the next request back to the native approval panel.

failureModes: A request that is no longer answerable (withdrawn) leaves both decisions disabled until the next request replaces the card.
A decision that does not reach the agent shows the failure under the details and unlocks the card to retry.
A remote thread's approval (multi-host) is not a native waterfall request and keeps its own panel.

externalDependencies.boundary: The decision, its waterfall and the request's one-answer lock belong to the native approval package; the card renders the request and calls answer().
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: src/approval-risk.test.ts rates the commands; the card renders in the composer chain the native approval package also registers.
